value: parabolic trough: single-axis tracking parabolic mirrors (arrays up to 100 m long, 5-6 m aperture) concentrate sunlight 60-80 times on an evacuated receiver tube on the focal line; synthetic oil (to 390 degC), steam or molten salt (to 550 degC) carries the heat to a steam generator; more than 90% of installed CSP

value: linear Fresnel reflector: rows of ground-level flat or slightly curved mirrors with single-axis tracking focus on a fixed receiver tube several metres above, often with a secondary mirror; water is evaporated directly to saturated steam (direct steam generation); cheaper mirrors but lower optical efficiency than trough; thermal storage harder with direct steam generation
note: The brief describes CSP as power plants (14-370 MWe); the collector field is what an industrial heat application would use. p.3 and p.6: CSP heat can serve industrial processes, desalination, enhanced oil recovery and refining, but the brief gives no heat-specific costs or performance.
